note: Encode every attacker-controlled interpolation before inserting it into an HTML sink. Escape ampersands first, then angle brackets and both quote characters, so legitimate text remains visible without becoming markup.
after:
const escapeHtml = value => String(value).replace(/[&<>"']/g, char => ({ '&': '&', '<': '<', '>': '>', '"': '"', "'": ''' })[char]); element.innerHTML = `

${escapeHtml(untrusted)}

`;
